sections.h2: Where do I find the Benzie County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Go to Suite 202 of the Government Center, 448 Court Place, Beulah, MI 49617. Doors are open weekdays, 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., and the office line is 231-882-0016.

Benzie County hugs Lake Michigan in the northwest of the Lower Peninsula, and its website advertises more than 100 lakes and several square miles of state forest. Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in those townships and in the city of Frankfort lands in the same index at this one counter.

  • Staff will not draft blank forms or offer legal opinions. For drafting, the office points people to an attorney or a title company.
  • Filing can happen at the counter, through the mail, by UPS or FedEx, or electronically.
  • A mailed copy request needs a stamped envelope addressed to yourself.

sections.h2: How much will Benzie County charge to record my paperwork?
sections.html:
According to the county, a document costs $30.00 to file whatever its length. State law in MCL 600.2567 sets the same $30 and folds the survey fee into it. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for every instrument past the first.

Benzie County recording office charges. Source: Benzie County Register of Deeds page and MCL 600.2567.
ServicePrice
File one document$30.00
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Copy of a recorded real estate record$1.00 a page
Certification of a document$5.00 extra
Tax certificate covering up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Every description beyond five20 cents

A tax certificate from the County Treasurer is needed for warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts and their assignments, and condominium master deeds. MCL 211.135 asks for proof of five years of paid taxes before the instrument date.

sections.h2: Can I record electronically in Benzie County, and is there a surcharge?
sections.html:
Electronic filing is accepted through four vendors named on the county page: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. Each vendor sets its own price. The Register of Deeds itself tacks on nothing.

When your deed also needs a county tax certification, the office steers filers to ePN, since it has built a document router with that company. One electronic submission can then cover both stops.

Looking up records is a different service. The index runs by grantor and grantee, and scanned images go back to the middle of the 1800s. A public search through the Tapestry link costs money, while title professionals can subscribe to Laredo. Phone the office to set up a subscription.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Benzie County deed?
sections.html:
The recording office gathers Michigan's state transfer tax when the deed is filed, and the county page links both the county statute (MCL 207.505) and the state statute (MCL 207.526). The state's rate is $3.75 per $500 of price, with part of a $500 block counted as a full block, which equals $7.50 per $1,000. Ask the office what county amount applies to your paper.

At the Census median home value for Benzie of $285,700, the state tax alone is $2,145: the price spans 572 blocks of $500 once rounded up. That amount deserves a line in any shoreline seller's net sheet.

The state act excuses certain transfers, and the deed must state the reason.

  • A price below $100, loan security papers, leases and mineral interests.
  • A gift deed running from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • A court order that names no money amount, a boundary line fix, or a quitclaim that repairs a defect in title.
  • A land contract still holding title with the seller, plus foreclosures and deeds given in place of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What kinds of instruments does Benzie County record?
sections.html:
The office lists its services as the recording of land related paper, and the list is broad. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or estate settlement.

  • Warranty, quit claim, mineral, administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages together with their assignments and discharges.
  • State and federal tax liens, circuit court orders and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most with an older loan. After a mortgage is satisfied, the lender files a discharge, and the buyer's title company looks for it in this index before clearing title.

sections.h2: What should a Benzie County seller do before filing a deed?
sections.html:
Sequence matters at a small counter. Begin with the title commitment, so you know which liens need a discharge. Then ask the Treasurer for the certificate if the deed has a warranty clause, or send the deed through ePN so certification is routed along with it. Next, confirm the full price on the deed, because transfer tax follows the stated price.

Finally, choose a delivery route. Walk it in during weekday counter hours, mail it with a return envelope, or have the closing agent file it electronically through one of the four vendors. For a family transfer, write the exemption on the face of the instrument so the tax is not collected by mistake.

sections.h2: Which neighbors of the Register of Deeds should a seller call?
sections.html:
The Treasurer sits on the upper level of the same building, phone 231-882-0011, and keeps the same weekday hours. That office runs the delinquent tax process under Public Act 206, holds the tax rolls, and accepts delinquent tax online with a 2.49 percent card fee (at least $1.50) or a flat $1.00 on e-checks.

Equalization is on the lower level in Suite 130, phone 231-882-0015. It provides parcel maps, descriptions, values, sales data, tax maps and millage rates, and it links to a parcel search plus FEMA map change forms, a useful stop for lakefront owners.

The Register chairs the county Plat Board for new subdivisions and also takes U.S. passport applications.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Benzie County housing?
sections.html:
Benzie is small and getting bigger. The 2025 estimate is 18,568 people, a 3.3 percent rise over the 2020 base, spread across 319.7 square miles of land. Residents 65 and over make up 31.1 percent of the population.

There are 12,682 housing units but only 7,708 households, and owners occupy 87.8 percent of homes. For 2020 to 2024, median value is $285,700 and median household income is $74,834. Permits for 136 new homes were issued in 2025. Because units outnumber households so widely, ask the title agent early whether any owner or heir lives out of the area, since that changes where papers are signed and mailed.

faqs.q: How much does Benzie County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document regardless of length. If a single paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each one beyond the first adds three dollars.

faqs.q: Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds add a surcharge for electronic filing?
faqs.a: No. Only the vendor you choose bills a fee. Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm are the approved companies.

faqs.q: When is a tax certificate required in Benzie County?
faqs.a: For warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds. It costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions, then 20 cents for each added description.

faqs.q: Will Benzie County staff write my deed for me?
faqs.a: They will not. The office neither prepares blank documents nor gives legal advice, so hire an attorney or use a title company.

faqs.q: What are the Benzie County Register of Deeds hours and phone number?
faqs.a: The counter is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., in Suite 202 of the Government Center in Beulah. The phone is 231-882-0016.
